headline: Choppy but ultimately flat session: KSE-100 opened around 173,500, sold off to an intraday low of 172,250 by midday on fresh Middle East escalation (Houthi strikes on Saudi cities, US strikes on Iranian oil tankers, Iran hitting a US base in Jordan, Brent nearing $100), then clawed most of it back through the afternoon to trade ~172,741 as of ~14:50 PKT (~+99pts / +0.06% vs Tuesday's close of 172,642.16) — a much calmer finish than the last two red sessions. No single holding moved >5% today and portfolio value is essentially breakeven (~Rs 10.256M, P/L ~-Rs 363, ~-0.00% on cost), so no notification went out on price/market grounds. Holdings check: index.html unchanged from last review — no off-app buys synced this time; AVN's EXIT call remains unexecuted (24,500 shares still held) through 11 reviews now, no new company news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 loss filing. One genuine catch-up item this review: Bestway Cement (BWCL) posted FY2026 results (year ended Jun 30) that hadn't been surfaced in prior reviews — consolidated profit +7.1% YoY to Rs 25.57B, EPS Rs 42.88 (vs Rs 40.02), and the board (at its Jul 22 meeting) recommended a Rs 10/share final dividend, taking the full-year payout to 400% of par vs 320% last year. The ex-date (Aug 24) and payment are already behind us and fully reflected in the current avg cost/price, so no dividend notification is due — but it's a genuine earnings result worth a mention: revenue and operating margins were actually softer (gross profit -12.9%, operating profit -17.1%) and the profit beat leaned on cost management/other income rather than core margin expansion, a pattern worth watching (much milder version of the AVN warning sign) even though the headline dividend raise is good news. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) is ~8.87% — essentially unchanged from yesterday's ~8.9%, still short of the 10% dry-powder trigger; today's recovery slowed the run toward that line rather than accelerating it. Entry levels reassessed: no changes — nothing broke monthly support or shifted fundamentals today.
market: KSE-100 had a volatile round-trip Wed Sep 9: opened near 173,500, fell to an intraday low of 172,250.20 (a further leg down from Tuesday's 993pt drop) as Iranian-backed Houthi forces struck several Saudi cities, US forces hit multiple Iran-linked oil tankers, and Iran struck a US base in Jordan — Brent crude pushed toward $100/bbl on the escalation. Selling was again broad (autos, cement, banks, fertiliser, OMCs; MARI/PSO/HBL/MCB/NBP/UBL all red in the morning) but the index recovered through the afternoon to ~172,741 by ~14:50 PKT, essentially flat to slightly positive vs Tuesday's close (+99pts/+0.06%) — the first session in three that didn't end deep red, even though the intraday move was sharper than the last two closes. Drawdown from the Jan 23 ATH (189,556) sits at ~8.87%, little changed from yesterday's ~8.9% — the fast narrowing seen Mon-Tue paused today; still below the 10% line that would justify shifting AICF/MICF cash into MZNPETF/MIIETF, worth checking daily while Hormuz/Gulf tensions stay this elevated. SBP holds at 11.5%; the next MPC meeting is Sep 14, 2026 (5 days away) — AHL's survey shows 87.5% of respondents expect no change, 12.5% expect a 50bps hike; CPI inflation has picked up to ~10.18% average in the first two months of FY27 (from 3.56% a year earlier), which is the main reason a hike is even on the table, though a hold remains the base case. Current account deficit narrowed 38% YoY to $328M in July; remittances +13% YoY to $3.6B; primary fiscal surplus 2.9% of GDP in FY26, above the IMF target — underlying macro backdrop still reasonably supportive despite the inflation uptick. DRAP drug-pricing review: unchanged from last review — pharma associations continue opposing the pricing-formula/Hardship Policy/Policy Board changes (still the Sep 4 story, nothing enacted since); GLAXO/SEARL stance unchanged (HOLD, watch into Q4). BWCL (new this review): FY2026 (year to Jun 30) consolidated profit +7.1% YoY to Rs 25.57B, EPS Rs 42.88 vs Rs 40.02 FY2025; board (Jul 22 meeting) recommended a Rs 10/share final dividend (total FY26 payout 400% vs 320% FY25); ex-date Aug 24, already paid — old news to the market but new to this review's coverage. Notably gross profit fell 12.9% and operating profit fell 17.1% on higher costs, so the profit growth came from cost management/other income, not core margin expansion — a mild version of the pattern that broke AVN's thesis, worth a watch-note even though BWCL's core business (unlike AVN's) is still solidly profitable and cash-generative. AVN — no new company announcements since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 loss filing; EXIT call unexecuted through 11 reviews now. DATA QUALITY: stock prices refreshed normally (~14:50 PKT, close to the 15:30 close). Fund NAVs (funds_updated: Aug 13) are now 27 days stale — the MUFAP scraper issue remains unresolved; ~28% of portfolio value (all 7 funds) is still being priced off a nearly month-old NAV snapshot, a growing blind spot needing a real fix.

actions.title: Avanceon — thesis still broken, EXIT call unexecuted through 11 reviews
actions.detail: No new news since the Aug 28 H1/Q2 FY26 filing: consolidated H1 2026 revenue grew +34% YoY but the company swung from a Rs 168M profit to a Rs 260M NET LOSS (EPS -Rs 0.62 vs +Rs 0.38); Q2 alone the loss widened to Rs 317M. No dividend declared. Admin/selling expenses up 45% YoY outpaced revenue growth, and a one-off 'other income' cushion from last year (Rs 162M) collapsed to Rs 77M this year, exposing weak core operating economics — real, board-confirmed deterioration, not a rumor. Now Rs 28.98 (-35.7% on cost), essentially flat today (+0.6%) after the broad market's morning dip mostly reversed. No earnings catalyst pending before Q3; there's no reason left to keep waiting. The Aug 25 EXIT call is unexecuted through 11 reviews now — recommend selling the entire position at market.
